turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Hi, thanks for hopping on today. This is Jordan from Sensi.AI — I know you're busy running the agency, so I'll try to keep this efficient. Before I dive in, can I ask how many caregivers you've got out in the field right now?

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Sure, we're at about 60 caregivers, covering maybe 140 clients across two counties.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Got it, that's a solid size. So what we do with Cally, our AI voice platform, is we place automated check-in calls to your clients or their caregivers after each shift, and it picks up on things like mood changes, missed medications, fall risk language — stuff that might otherwise slip through the cracks until a family member calls in upset. It basically gives you an early warning system.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Okay, and how does that actually work — is it replacing the caregiver's own notes, or on top of it?

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: It's on top of it, so nothing changes for your caregivers day to day. Cally just calls after the visit, has a short natural conversation, and then flags anything concerning to your office staff through a dashboard. Honestly the big thing agencies love is the early detection piece — we've had agencies catch a UTI starting to develop just from the voice sentiment analysis before it turned into a hospital visit. That's kind of our headline stat, it's been huge for agencies trying to reduce readmissions.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: That's interesting. We actually just had a family pull their mom out of our care last month because nobody caught that she'd stopped eating for like four days.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Yeah, that's exactly the kind of gap we're trying to close. So with Cally in place, those calls would happen daily or every few days depending on how you set the cadence, and any red flags — mood, appetite, anything unusual — get surfaced right away instead of waiting for the next in-person visit.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Makes sense. What's the actual setup like on our end — do we need new hardware, training for staff?

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: No hardware at all, it's fully phone-based, so no apps for your caregivers or clients to download. Onboarding is mostly just us loading in your client roster and setting call preferences. Most agencies are live within a couple weeks. And again, the readmission piece is really the anchor value here — agencies using Sensi have reported meaningful drops in hospital readmissions just from catching these early signals through the voice check-ins.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Yeah, you mentioned that a couple times. I get it, it's a strong stat.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: It really is, it's probably our best proof point across the client base. But I know every agency's different — what's driving you to look at something like this right now?

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Honestly it's a mix — some family complaints, and we've had some caregiver turnover so oversight has been thinner than usual.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Totally understand, staffing churn makes consistent oversight tough. That's actually one of the reasons agencies lean on Cally, because it doesn't depend on which caregiver is covering a shift — the check-in call happens no matter who's on. So even during turnover periods you've still got that layer of visibility.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Right, that would help with the family complaints piece too, probably, since they'd see we're staying on top of things.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Yeah, for sure. So typically what we'd do next is get you set up with a short pilot on maybe 20 or 30 clients, just so your team can see the flags coming through and how the dashboard works before rolling it out agency-wide.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Okay. What's pricing look like for something like that?

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: It scales with number of clients monitored, so I'd want to put together a proposal based on your actual client count rather than throw out a number that doesn't fit. I can pull that together along with a one-pager on the readmission data I mentioned.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Sure, that'd be helpful to see.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Great, I'll get that packet together — pricing breakdown, the case study on readmissions, and a quick overview of the pilot process.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Sounds good, I'll take a look when you send it.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Perfect, I'll send that over in the next day or two. Anything specific you want me to make sure is included?

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Maybe something on how it handles families who don't speak English as a first language — we've got a decent number of those clients.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Good call, I'll see what I can find on that and include it. I'll follow up once it's in your inbox.

turns.speaker: Prospect
turns.text: Sounds good, talk soon.

turns.speaker: Rep
turns.text: Thanks for your time today, I'll be in touch.
